To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a first-order phase transition is possible even without supersymmetry and without the need to fine-tune parameters of the model, (ii) the phase transition is driven by the top quarks and stops and is thus sensitive to the stop mass and the top Yukawa coupling, (iii) the top quark plays the role of the higgsinos and the stops play the role of the gauginos in this non-supersymmetric model.

the two-Higgs-doublet model with softly broken CP symmetry can provide a successful electroweak bariogenesis mechanism, where the top quark takes over the role of Higgsinos in supersymmetric models, and where the phase transition is strongly first-order and occurs above the critical temperature for sphaleron processes, and the baryon asymmetries are generated by the top quark.
the baryon asymmetries of the Universe can be explained by electroweak beryogenesis in the 2HDM.
